subject: RW-Temporal: elevated timeouts and partial failures — initial notice and mitigation
thread_summary: Initial detection of elevated 5xx/timeouts for RW-Temporal on long-context workloads; temporary fallbacks applied, rollback scheduled; customer notified and postmortem planned.
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@stellardata.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T15:12:00Z
Subject: RW-Temporal: elevated timeouts and partial failures — initial notice and mitigation

Hi Alex,

I want to make you aware of an ongoing issue affecting a subset of requests served by the RW-Temporal family (large-context variants) that started at ~2027-05-30T14:50Z. We're seeing an increase in timeouts and 5xx responses for requests with >6k token contexts — roughly 6-9% of traffic for RW-Temporal in your account appears affected based on our initial sampling.

What we're doing now:
- Immediate mitigation: traffic routed automatically to RW-Compact fallback for new requests that match the failing profile.
- Rate-limiting: temporary per-project throttling applied to reduce retry storms.
- Telemetry: collected detailed logs and an impact map attached.

Next steps and ETA:
- Our SREs are running a targeted analysis now; we expect the first technical update within 120 minutes and a planned rollback if the suspect kernel change is confirmed.
- If rollback proceeds, we expect a brief maintenance window (~10-20 minutes) during which a small percentage of requests may see elevated latency.

Attachments: rw-temporal-error-log-20270530.tar.gz (log bundle), customer-impact-map-20270530.csv

Apologies for the disruption — I'm copying Marcus and Marissa for technical context and will provide hourly updates until this is resolved.

Regards,
Olga
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: rw-temporal-error-log-20270530.tar.gz (log bundle, 14MB)]

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@stellardata.com>

Date: 2027-05-30T15:29:00Z
Subject: Re: RW-Temporal: elevated timeouts and partial failures — initial notice and mitigation

Thanks for the heads up, Olga.

We started seeing errors around 14:52Z — our downstream retries caused some increased latencies in our orchestration layer. From our end impact is roughly: 10% failed calls for model rw-temporal-large, primarily on long-context summarization jobs. We do have data on request IDs and timestamps; I can share a small sample if that helps.

Two quick asks:
1) Can you confirm whether any token-level outputs were lost or truncated for our successful fallback responses?
2) ETA on the rollback if that becomes the path forward — our ops team needs to schedule a rolling deploy window.

Appreciate the quick action.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-31T02:06:00Z
Subject: RE: RW-Temporal incident — preliminary technical notes

Team — preliminary findings from the overnight trace:

- Symptom: gradual memory growth in the attention KV cache path when sequence length > 6k under the new attention kernel shipped 2027-05-29. This leads to intermittent OOMs in inference worker processes and subsequent 5xx responses.
- Trigger surface: requests with long static prefixes and sustained streaming create cache pressure; retention/eviction behaviour appears altered by the kernel change.

Mitigations tested in staging:
- Patch A: conservative eviction adjustment + guardrail to cap KV cache per-request (candidate attached: rollback-patch-diff-05031.diff).
- Fallback: routing to RW-Compact avoids the slow path and reduces per-token memory; already applied in prod for affected requests.

Recommendation: controlled rollback of the kernel change with canary on 10% traffic, monitor for 2 hours, then ramp to 100% if stable. Rolling rollback should reduce failures materially within one maintenance window.

I'll prepare the rollback script and coordinate with SRE (Dylan) for the window.

— Marcus
Principal Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: rollback-patch-diff-05031.diff]

Schedule: 2027-06-01 22:00 UTC (start) — estimated 15 minutes to complete the canary and a full ramp by 22:30 UTC.
Expected impact: brief elevated latency and a <10% probability of transient 5xx during the switch; overall failure rate should drop to baseline once rollback completes.

Links and artifacts:
- Live incident docket: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/INC-20270530-RW-TEMPORAL
- Support ticket (HubSpot): https://hubspot.company/contacts/ACCT-9582

Thanks for your patience — we aim to keep disruption minimal.

Olga

Date: 2027-06-02T23:05:00Z
Subject: Postmortem draft and customer follow-ups — RW-Temporal incident

Folks — draft postmortem notes and action items for the RW-Temporal incident. Please review and add owners by EOD tomorrow. I'll circulate the external-facing postmortem to StellarData once we have the final approval.

Summary:
- Incident: elevated 5xx/timeouts for RW-Temporal large-context variants caused by a memory regression in the new attention kernel (deploy 2027-05-29).
- Impact: affected ~6-10% of RW-Temporal traffic for StellarData between 2027-05-30T14:50Z and 2027-06-01T22:15Z.
- Mitigation: temporary fallback to RW-Compact; controlled rollback of kernel change completed 2027-06-01 22:20 UTC.

Action items (owners):
1) SRE: finalize leak proof test harness and add regression test for KV cache size (owner: Dylan) — due 2027-06-10.
2) Runtime: add per-model telemetry on KV cache retention + alert thresholds (owner: Marcus) — due 2027-06-14.
3) Customer Success: draft customer-facing postmortem and credits proposal (owner: Marissa) — due 2027-06-05.

Attachments referenced: rw-temporal-error-log-20270530.tar.gz, customer-impact-map-20270530.csv, rollback-patch-diff-05031.diff

I'll publish a single consolidated postmortem to the Confluence link and share a short summary to StellarData by 2027-06-04.

Regards,
Olga
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
